title: IPTG-induced Overexpression in E. coli
author: Igem Dusseldorf
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8ffhtjn

steps.title: Inoculate LB culture
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of overnight E. coli culture to 100 ml LB containing ampicillin and grow at 37 °C, 180 rpm until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.6.

steps.title: Induce protein expression
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of 1 M IPTG stock to achieve a final concentration of 0.5 mM, then incubate for 2 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture for 10 min at 4000 × g, 4 °C; discard the supernatant and store the cell pellet at –80 °C.

steps.title: Thaw cell pellet
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen cell pellet on ice.

steps.title: Resuspend in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml ice‑cold water (up to two 50 ml pellets from a 100 ml culture may be combined), transfer to 2 ml reaction tubes, centrifuge at the maximum speed of a desktop centrifuge at 4 °C for 15 min, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Extract inclusion bodies with BPER
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 ml BPER, vortex, then vortex again every 2 min for a total of 15 min; centrifuge at the maximum speed of a desktop centrifuge at 4 °C for 15 min and keep the supernatant (BPER) on ice in separate tubes.

steps.title: Prepare 1/10 BPER wash
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 ml BPER with 9 ml water to make 1/10 BPER.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 1/10 BPER
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml 1/10 BPER to the pellet, vortex for three cycles of 1 min each, centrifuge at the maximum speed of a desktop centrifuge at 4 °C for 15 min, and keep the supernatant (1/10 BPER) on ice in separate tubes.

steps.title: Final resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in 200 µl of 50 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 150 mM KCl, 10 % glycerol (water may be used instead if activity assays are not required).

steps.title: Analyze or store protein
steps.instruction: Either mix 0.5–1 µl of the sample with 4 µl 5× SDS buffer and load onto an SDS‑PAGE gel, or store the resuspended protein at –20 °C.
